r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Built and ran my own falsifiers, independent of the implementer's, for every family. (1) HOLE_RATIO_CEILING=0.90 vs measured 0.673: disabled docstring emission only in extract.Extractor._func -- the SHARED code path for visit_FunctionDef AND visit_AsyncFunctionDef (both = _func), which covers plain functions AND methods but not visit_ClassDef's separate docstring emission. This is a realistic, scoped single-function-path bug, not a contrived global break. Rebuilt the real repo through the mutated package: holes/entities = 3537/3793 = 0.933, crossing 0.90. The ceiling fires on a plausible partial regression, not only on a maximal catastrophe. (2) CHURN ceilings=3.0 vs measured 1.27x/1.02x: ran 3 independent synthetic variants on a NEW 2-callee-per-caller fixture (reorder-inducing rename, non-reordering rename, short-to-much-longer-name rename) -- all three landed at the SAME 1.545 ratio, confirming render.tally()'s comma-joined single line means neither sort-position changes nor length changes split one call-site mention into multiple diff lines. Also ran an INDEPENDENT real-corpus rename via isolated git worktree (checklist_engine.EngineError -> EngineFault, an 80-call-site PRODUCTION symbol, not the implementer's test symbol), restricted to the mappable corpus via discovery.discover_corpus: 174 map diff lines / 348 source diff lines = 0.5x. Both real-corpus renames (implementer's 212-caller test symbol at 1.02x, mine at 80-caller production symbol at 0.5x) and my worst synthetic case (1.545x) stay well under 3.0 -- no realistic rename shape tested here approaches the ceiling. (3) RECALL_FLOORS: confirmed by reading RecallFloorTests.setUpClass that it builds and measures ONLY the synthetic _make_recall_fixture_repo, never ROOT -- the floor cannot fire against ordinary live-corpus change. The writes-recall-derivation-honesty claim is independently corroborated: DESIGN_SPEC.md line 247 (critic TS7) records 'the SCIP oracle is blind to writes' as the reason for the accepted hand-labeled-sample fix, and extract.py's own module docstring has stated 'stdlib only... No SCIP' since g0 -- so 'no automated oracle backs ANY predicate' is a verifiable fact, not just an assertion. (4) TEMPLATE_ASCII_INVARIANT: ran two of my own mutations distinct from the implementer's -- (a) non-ASCII spliced into TEST_NOTE (not the implementer's REFS_LEGEND target): caught. (b) non-ASCII spliced into module_index's own FUNCTION DOCSTRING: correctly NOT flagged, proving the docstring-exclusion branch is real, not vacuous -- a gap in the implementer's own falsifier suite, which never exercises this branch with real non-ASCII docstring text (their second falsifier test only proves f-string INTERPOLATION is excluded, a different and automatic AST property). Confirmed baseline render.py currently authors zero non-ASCII template literals, which combined with the 386 existing non-ASCII pages proves by construction those 386 pages' non-ASCII text cannot originate from render.py's own literals. (5) Reproduced independently: full suite 1793 passed/2 skipped/672 subtests/0 failed exit 0 (385.97s); closing selector -k 'baseline or churn or recall or ascii' on tests/test_code_map.py: 13 passed exit 0; fresh build+check: 7/7 exit 0. One gap found and routed to r4: CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME's own docstring block never states its own WHEN THIS FIRES action line (only CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_LOCAL_EDIT does), against the gate's explicit constraint that every threshold state one.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: gate-spec.json's gb constraints require: no absolute-count thresholds (PASS -- all four families are ratios or an invariant); the FULL suite green at the boundary (PASS -- independently reproduced 1793p/2s/672 subtests/0f); and Tommy's ruling that every threshold committed here must state, in one line, what a human should DO when it fires ('a tripwire with no action is noise'). Three of the four families comply: HOLE_RATIO_CEILING, CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_LOCAL_EDIT, RECALL_FLOORS and TEMPLATE_ASCII_INVARIANT each carry an explicit 'WHEN THIS FIRES:' line. CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME does not -- its docstring block (thresholds.py lines 47-59) documents the measurement and the structural 1-line-per-call-site reasoning but never states an action distinct from (or referring back to) CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_LOCAL_EDIT's. A reader can infer the same numeric ceiling implies a related diagnostic, but the rename failure mode is not the same as the local-edit one (LOCAL_EDIT's stated action -- 'look for a page that changed without its entity changing, a rendering instability' -- describes a different symptom than a rename-driven blowup would show), so the inference is not safe to leave implicit. This is a narrow, cheap-to-fix gap against an explicit, named gate constraint, not a threshold-design defect: the ceiling itself is well-supported (see r3-evidence).

r7-recheck.title: Re-verify Commander's direct fix to CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME
r7-recheck.imperative: Commander added a WHEN THIS FIRES line to CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME directly (not via a remediation crew) to close the r4-quality blocker. Independently verify: (1) the added line is actionable and distinct from the local-edit ceiling's symptom; (2) the diff is purely additive (no logic change); (3) full suite + fresh build/check still pass; (4) the missing-action-line scan across all thresholds was exhaustive. Record pass/fail with a finding; this is NOT a self-grade since Commander authored the fix.
r7-recheck.finding: (1) Actionability -- my independent read, not agreement: the added line names a distinct symptom (map diff lines exceed call-site count -- explicitly contrasted with LOCAL_EDIT's rendering-instability symptom) and two concrete things to open: the renamed symbol's own caller-list line (check in-place edit vs rewrap/re-sort) and a page-path collision with an existing symbol name. Both are grounded in the actual mechanism (render.tally()'s single comma-joined line, and the page-path collision surface this review already probed) -- this is comparably concrete to the other three WHEN THIS FIRES lines, not investigate-this noise. Satisfies the constraint. (2) git diff 3a9b4495 -- scripts/code_map/thresholds.py: purely additive, 8 new comment lines inserted before CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME = 3.0, zero logic change, zero other file touched (confirmed by git status: only thresholds.py plus Commander's own execute.json tracking dirty). File is pure ASCII (str.isascii() True) and ast.parse succeeds. (3) Full suite independently reproduced post-fix: 1793 passed, 2 skipped, 672 subtests passed, exit 0, 386.24s -- identical counts to the pre-fix baseline, confirming a documentation-only change caused no regression. Fresh build then check (run in that order, post-fix): build exit 0 (3793 entities, matches pre-fix); check 7/7 all ok (no-empty-pages, page-accounting, refs-line-self-consistent, entity-symbol-join, page-location-matches-content, inbound-attribution, deterministic-rebuild). Closing selector: 13 passed, exit 0. (4) Exhaustive re-scan, mechanically verified via grep correlating every 'WHEN THIS FIRES' occurrence against every top-level constant definition in thresholds.py: 6 top-level constants total. 5 are actual thresholds a test checks against (HOLE_RATIO_CEILING, CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_LOCAL_EDIT, CHURN_RATIO_CEILING_RENAME, RECALL_FLOORS, TEMPLATE_ASCII_INVARIANT) -- all 5 now immediately preceded by their own WHEN THIS FIRES line, 1:1. The 6th, RECALL_FLOOR_DERIVATION, is not itself a checked threshold (no test asserts against it), so it is correctly outside this constraint's scope -- my original pass was exhaustive against all checked thresholds, not partial. RECALL_FLOOR_DERIVATION grep (scripts/, tests/, all .py/.md, excluding __pycache__): 5 total hits repo-wide -- 1 is its own definition (thresholds.py:90), 0 are consumers in scripts/ or tests/, 1 is the code_map's own auto-generated INDEX.md page cataloging the symbol (not a functional reader -- the map catalogs every symbol whether used or not), 3 are this review's own artifacts. Genuinely dead: zero consumers. Precision for the record, per Commander's request to file this accurately rather than softly: this is NOT the same defect class as an unstated derivation. The load-bearing derivation the handoff cared about (why writes has no SCIP-independent oracle) IS stated, and IS what a human reads -- it lives in RECALL_FLOORS's own docstring comment two lines above (lines 72-79), which RECALL_FLOORS's WHEN THIS FIRES line points an investigator toward. RECALL_FLOOR_DERIVATION is a near-verbatim, unconsumed restatement of that same docstring (compared side by side: both say hand-labeled fixture, no automated oracle, writes derived the same way as calls/reads, stated rather than left implicit). The defect is duplication with silent-drift risk (nothing keeps the two copies in sync, so they could diverge unnoticed), not a missing or dishonest derivation. Remains triage candidate tc1, filed with this precision.
